description: Figure 3d, located in the bottom right quadrant of the 4-plot grid and captioned "AGNews clean-label," illustrates the performance of different trigger words on the AGNews dataset under a clean-label poisoning scenario with a 10% poison rate (2.5% of total samples). The vertical axis represents the Attack Success Rate (ASR), ranging from 0.5 to 0.9. The horizontal axis lists trigger words—"cf", "bb", "WNBA", "ESPN", "NHL", "FIFA", "Estadio", and "athletics"—arranged in ascending order according to the ASR of the clean model. Three distinct lines, each with a unique color and marker, depict the ASR for triggers inserted at different positions: a green line with circle markers for "start" position, an orange line with 'x' markers for "random" position, and a purple line with circle markers for "end" position. The green "start" line begins at an ASR of approximately 0.77 for "cf", dips to 0.50 for "bb", peaks at 0.90 for "WNBA", and ends at 0.90 for "athletics". The orange "random" line starts at 0.67 for "cf", drops to 0.50 for "bb", rises to 0.88 for "WNBA", and concludes at 0.86 for "athletics". The purple "end" line begins at 0.75 for "cf", falls to 0.57 for "bb", peaks at 0.92 for "WNBA", and ends at 0.83 for "athletics". All three lines exhibit a general upward trend across the x-axis, with the "start" and "end" positions showing higher ASR values than the "random" position for most trigger words.
